sec: The primary problems and the three reading methods · p827

items.q: The ‘primary problem’ tree of ABG interpretation ends in how many primary abnormalities?
opts: Four — metabolic acidosis, metabolic alkalosis, respiratory acidosis, respiratory alkalosis
Six — each of the four with acute and chronic forms
items.exp: The tree gives four primary problems: metabolic acidosis and metabolic alkalosis (bicarbonate arms) and respiratory acidosis and alkalosis (PaCO₂ arms). (Book p827)

items.q: Match the respiratory arms of the primary-problem tree — 1) Respiratory acidosis  2) Respiratory alkalosis  3) Each respiratory disorder is further labelled … A) Acute or chronic  B) ↑PaCO₂  C) ↓PaCO₂
items.exp: Respiratory acidosis ↑PaCO₂ and respiratory alkalosis ↓PaCO₂; both branches are further divided into acute and chronic forms. (Book p827)

items.q: ‘In the primary-problem tree, only the respiratory disorders are further divided into acute and chronic.’
opts: True — the acute/chronic bracket sits under the two respiratory arms
False — the metabolic arms are also divided into acute and chronic
False — no arm is divided into acute and chronic
True, but the metabolic arms are divided into compensated and uncompensated instead
items.exp: The printed tree brackets the two respiratory arms together with ‘Acute’ and ‘Chronic’. (Book p827)

items.q: Match the ABG reading methods printed — 1) Boston  2) Copenhagen  3) Stewarts … A) Third-listed method  B) First-listed method  C) Second-listed method
items.exp: ABG reading methods listed left to right: Boston, Copenhagen, Stewarts. (Book p827)

items.q: ‘On p827 the metabolic arms are drawn as “metabolic acidosis ↑HCO₃⁻” and “metabolic alkalosis ↓HCO₃⁻”, while the step-2 flowchart on p828 gives ↓HCO₃⁻ for metabolic acidosis and ↑HCO₃⁻ for metabolic alkalosis.’
opts: True — the two pages place the metabolic arrows differently, and p828 carries the interpretation logic
False — both pages draw ↑HCO₃⁻ under metabolic acidosis
False — both pages draw ↓HCO₃⁻ under metabolic acidosis
False — the p828 flowchart never mentions HCO₃⁻
items.exp: The p827 primary-problem tree prints the bicarbonate arrows under the metabolic labels in the reverse sense, whereas the step-2 flowchart on p828 uses ↓HCO₃⁻ = metabolic acidosis and ↑HCO₃⁻ = metabolic alkalosis — the convention followed when interpreting a report. (Book p827)

items.q: All but one of the following are printed ABG reading methods. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Only three reading methods are listed — Boston, Copenhagen and Stewarts. (Book p827)

items.q: An ABG report shows pH 7.30 with a high PaCO₂ and a high HCO₃⁻. Using the primary-problem tree, which arm is being reported?
opts: Respiratory acidosis, to be labelled acute or chronic
Respiratory alkalosis, to be labelled acute or chronic
Mixed metabolic acidosis and metabolic alkalosis
items.exp: A high PaCO₂ places the report on the respiratory-acidosis arm of the tree, which is then labelled acute or chronic. (Book p827)
